clue.text: Petition therefore within the law

parts.note: so means therefore, as in 'it rained, so we left'
licit means lawful, the opposite of illicit

explanation.surface: Someone lodges a petition, confident it is legally sound.
explanation.definitionFit: To petition someone is to ask earnestly for something, a verb synonym.

clue.text: He delivers cutting remark about wife with hesitation

indicators.note: about means around, so the word for remark surrounds the abbreviation

parts.note: to say is to remark
er is a hesitant sound in speech

explanation.surface: A man makes a hurtful comment about his wife, haltingly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cutting remark' reads as a phrase, but 'cutting' belongs to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A sawyer is a worker who saws timber, one who performs cutting.

clue.text: American soldier visiting upset Christmas host

indicators.note: visiting means staying inside, so the soldier goes within the festive word
upset in a down clue means turned upside down, so the festive word is read backwards

parts.note: Noel is a name for Christmas
GI is a US soldier

explanation.surface: A US soldier drops in on a host whose Christmas has gone wrong.
explanation.walkthrough: 'host' is a multitude here, not someone entertaining guests; in a down clue 'upset' turns the festive word over to LEON.
explanation.definitionFit: A host is a vast number, as is a legion, as in 'their name is legion'.

clue.text: Fletcher — an ungainly footballer

indicators.note: ungainly means awkward and clumsy, so the letters lurch into a new order

explanation.surface: A footballer named Fletcher is clumsy on the pitch.
explanation.definitionFit: A defender playing in the middle of the back line, a football position.

clue.text: Lady's partner married in horse-drawn vehicle

indicators.note: in places the abbreviation inside the word for the carriage

parts.note: a trap is a light two-wheeled carriage pulled by a horse

explanation.surface: A newly married couple ride off in a pony carriage.
explanation.definitionFit: In Disney's Lady and the Tramp, the stray dog is Lady's companion, a cultural reference.

clue.text: Lots in detective team coming back with force

indicators.note: coming back tells us to read the whole assembled group of letters backwards
in places the word for lots inside the detective team's letters

parts.note: CID is the Criminal Investigation Department, the British police detective branch
lots means many

explanation.surface: A big police squad returns in strength.
explanation.walkthrough: 'coming back' reverses the whole assembly, CIMANYD, not just the detective team.
explanation.definitionFit: Something full of energy and power acts forcefully, so the adjective matches the phrase.

clue.text: Some French fiend and a tragic heroine

parts.note: des is French for some
a demon is a fiend
the A is taken as written

explanation.surface: French villains and a doomed heroine in a melodrama.
explanation.definitionFit: Othello's wife, killed by him in Shakespeare's tragedy, is a classic tragic heroine.

clue.text: Well-groomed cattle

definitions.meaning: an old word for oxen or bovine animals, as in neatherd

explanation.surface: Tidy livestock at a show.
explanation.definitionFit: One sense is trim and tidy; the other is an archaic collective word for cattle.

clue.text: Chap having audacity to strike grand official

parts.note: a chap is a man

indicators.note: to strike means to strike out, so the letter for grand is removed

parts.note: daring means bold, having audacity
G is the abbreviation for a grand, a thousand pounds

explanation.surface: A bold man dares to hit an important official.
explanation.definitionFit: A mandarin was a high Chinese official; now any senior civil servant.

clue.text: Naval vessel runs old fighter into shelter built for fliers

indicators.note: into places the runs letter and the old soldier inside the shelter word

parts.note: a cote is a shelter for doves or pigeons
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs
vet is short for veteran, an old soldier

explanation.surface: A warship drives an aged combat plane into an aircraft hangar.
explanation.definitionFit: A corvette is a small escort warship, a type of naval vessel.

clue.text: Lorry to continue shaking

parts.note: to wag is to shake to and fro, as a dog's tail does
on is an instruction to carry on, as in 'on with the show'

explanation.surface: A truck keeps rattling along.
explanation.definitionFit: A wagon is a goods vehicle, so it is a fair synonym for a truck or lorry.

clue.text: A British composer, one staying on the 9

parts.note: Sir John Stainer was an English composer of church music, best known for The Crucifixion

explanation.surface: A British composer remains loyal to some vehicle mentioned at 9.
explanation.walkthrough: The 9 refers to the answer at 9 across, a lorry; being 'on the wagon' means not drinking alcohol.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone on the wagon refuses alcohol, so they are a teetotaller by idiom.

clue.text: European caught notorious criminal — one with high self-opinion

parts.note: got means caught, as in 'the police got him'
Jack the Ripper, the notorious unidentified Victorian murderer in London

explanation.surface: A European arrests an infamous villain and becomes insufferably smug.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who indulges in self-glorifying acts is vain and full of their own importance.

clue.text: Mere elk roaming around area

indicators.note: around means the scrambled animal letters wrap themselves round the abbreviation
roaming means wandering, so the letters of the animal word wander into a new order

explanation.surface: Just an elk wandering about some patch of land.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mere' looks like 'only', but it is the noun. 'roaming' turns ELK into LKE, and A goes inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A mere is a small body of standing water, chiefly in poetry or English place names.

clue.text: Group of Nicaraguan rebel fighters? It's run illegally

parts.note: the Contras were rebels fighting Nicaragua's Sandinista government in the 1980s
a band is a group

explanation.surface: A question about a guerrilla group that operates outside the law.
explanation.definitionFit: Goods that are smuggled, run past customs, are illicit goods.

clue.text: Old scientist treated English troop

indicators.note: treated in the sense of processed or worked on, so the letters are reworked

explanation.surface: An elderly scientist attended to a body of English soldiers.
explanation.definitionFit: Phrenology, reading character from skull bumps, was a nineteenth-century discipline long since abandoned.

clue.text: Race in the bustling business centre

indicators.note: bustling means busily moving about, so the letters jostle into a new order

parts.note: the City is London's financial district, the business centre

explanation.surface: A race happening in a busy commercial district.
explanation.definitionFit: Race in the sense of a shared ethnic background or descent.

clue.text: Dumps Labrador perhaps

definitions.meaning: low spirits, as in 'down in the dumps'
an example of a dark-coated canine; Labradors can be dark

explanation.surface: A Labrador maybe drops something off.
explanation.definitionFit: Churchill's name for depression, and literally a dark-coloured dog such as a Labrador.

clue.text: In time, great flows from the south becoming essential

indicators.note: flowing from the south in a down clue means moving upwards, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: large means great

explanation.surface: Over time, a great river rising from the south becomes vital.
explanation.definitionFit: Integral means fundamental or necessary to the whole, a synonym.

clue.text: Really honest bubbly people seeking mates

indicators.note: bubbly suggests fizzing and effervescing, so the letters froth into a new order

explanation.surface: Sincere, vivacious singles hoping to find a partner, as in a dating advert.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom names those who place personal adverts looking for romance or partners.

clue.text: Work with relief manager after this person turned up

indicators.note: after places the manager word following the reversed pronoun
turned up in a down clue means reversed, read bottom to top

parts.note: this person is the writer, the setter, so me
a boss is a manager

explanation.surface: The manager arrives after me, relieved at the work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'relief' here is relief carving, raised design.
explanation.definitionFit: To raise a design on a surface is to create raised relief work.

clue.text: Drink of type unknown

parts.note: a brand is a kind or type
Y is an algebraic unknown

explanation.surface: A beverage of uncertain variety.
explanation.definitionFit: A spirit distilled from wine, a kind of alcoholic drink.

clue.text: Team triumphed

definitions.meaning: a group working together, such as a ship's company or rowing squad
an old past tense of crow, meaning exulted or boasted over a win

explanation.surface: A sports report: the side won.
explanation.definitionFit: One sense is a working group; the other is an archaic past tense of crow, to gloat.

clue.text: Record not so strong I put in denial of responsibility

parts.note: a disc is a gramophone record

indicators.note: put in tells us to place the letter I inside the word for weaker

parts.note: lamer means weaker, as of a feeble excuse

explanation.surface: A weaker argument is filed on record, but I deny all blame.
explanation.definitionFit: A formal statement rejecting liability or responsibility for something.

clue.text: Elite athlete once running round East

indicators.note: running round means circling, so the athlete's name encloses the compass letter

parts.note: Steve Cram is a former British middle-distance runner

explanation.surface: A top former athlete jogs around the eastern area.
explanation.definitionFit: The cream of something is its best part, the elite.

clue.text: Top marks picked up by expert

indicators.note: picked up by means collected inside, so the abbreviation goes within the expert word

parts.note: an ace is an expert
M is the abbreviation for marks, the old German currency

explanation.surface: Top grades gathered by a specialist.
explanation.definitionFit: The peak or highest point of achievement, a synonym for top.

clue.text: Instruction providing unfavourable information about the City I have to follow

indicators.note: to follow tells us this contraction comes after the earlier pieces
about means surrounding, so the scandal word goes round the postcode

parts.note: dirt is scandalous information, as in 'digging up dirt'
EC is the postal district of the City of London, its financial centre
I've is the contraction of I have

explanation.surface: An order supplying damaging gossip on London's financial district.
explanation.definitionFit: An official order or command given by an authority is a synonym for an instruction.

clue.text: A party gets navy on deck

parts.note: a do is an informal word for a party
RN is the Royal Navy

explanation.surface: At a party, the sailors arrive on the ship's deck.
explanation.walkthrough: 'deck' looks nautical next to 'navy', but it is the verb meaning to decorate.
explanation.definitionFit: To deck a hall is to decorate it, a verb synonym.

clue.text: People watching rowing boat crossing river

indicators.note: crossing here means spanning across, so the boat word straddles the river letter

parts.note: a galley is a ship propelled by oars

explanation.surface: Spectators watch a galley crossing a river.
explanation.definitionFit: The top balcony of a theatre, and by extension its audience, the onlookers.

clue.text: I'm surprised, keeping poems by Tennyson originally in reserve

indicators.note: keeping means holding inside, so the exclamation encloses the other pieces

parts.note: my! is an exclamation of surprise
odes are lyric poems

indicators.note: originally points to the first letter of the poet's name

explanation.surface: Amazed to find Tennyson's poems held back in storage.
explanation.definitionFit: Reserve as a character trait means restraint and lack of showiness, a synonym.
